w: Swamishri inaugurated and performed the murti-pratishtha of the Swaminarayan Mandir, Sankari

To do little and gain more is a gambler's tendency. To do wrong work and gain more money is a gambler's tendency. To labor for less than 8 hours at work or business and desire for more money is a gambler's tendency.
To take more in return for less effort does not please God.

In the evening Kishore Day assembly, the kishores performed an impressive folkdance on the glory of the Swaminarayan Mahamantra and a drama 'Hraday hraday na setu'. In conclusion, Swamishri addressed the kishores emphasizing the need and importance of satsang.
A devotee had come to Pramukh Swami Maharaj with both his sons.
One said, "I am studying to be a doctor."
"Good, good. Study well. But how about eating and drinking (alcohol and meat)?"
"It goes on."
Swamishri said, "You may not accept what we say from a spiritual point of view, but think from a medical point of view: is drinking a good thing?"
"No."
"Then what need is there at all to put into your body something that harms it? You are studying to be a doctor; we should not need to tell you much. Do you have any thought of giving it up?"
Before he could answer, Swamishri asked his father, "Do you take it?" The devotee said, "Now and then, on occasions, I end up taking it."

"Then what advice can I give him? He will argue back with me: first make him give it up, then talk to me. What can I say to him? You are educated. Is there any need for this? Why keep pouring it in needlessly? And where is it that one simply must drink? Does our work not get done without parties?" Swamishri asked many questions of this kind.
The devotee said, "What you say is true."

Full of compassion, Swamishri said, "You have been serving God for years, so we too should give you something, shouldn't we! We give you this: keep your life pure. If your body, values and culture all remain good, then this will continue into your later generations too, and your generations will also be happy."
A devotee who had come with them said, "Bapa! Bless him that he gives it all up."
Swamishri said, "If he stands up and receives it, then I will give it!"

The devotee was perhaps still struggling in his mind, but hearing Swamishri's words he stood up and went close to Swamishri. Blessing him, Swamishri said, "Thousands and billions of people can live without alcohol and meat. But it has become a fashion that because we have come to this country we must take it. There is nothing of the kind. Even if you do take it, these white people will not consider you one of their own. We should preserve our family dignity."

Nothing remained for the devotee to say. Swamishri gave vartman to each of them, and even while giving the water into their hands Swamishri kept saying, "We do all our work, but whatever is useless, remove it. We must preserve India's culture. It is fine that we have come here to earn money, but we should not run up a debt of our values, culture and spirituality. We have not come here to give them up; preserve them."

ds.t: No limit to his patience and compassion!
w: A youth came to Pramukh Swami Maharaj. One button of his shirt was open, and through it a gold chain around his neck could be seen. There was a certain carelessness in the way he walked. Red veins stood out in his eyes. Standing carelessly before Swamishri, he said, "Bapa! Let me tell you straight... I chew tobacco, I drink alcohol. Today I want to give it all up." He was talking with Swamishri while looking at the man who had come with him. Swamishri saw through him. Swamishri said, "It is right that you talk of giving all this up, but you are not saying it now under the influence of alcohol, are you!"

In fact he was speaking under the influence of alcohol. The smell of alcohol kept coming from his mouth. He said, "Oh, come on! Bapji, I really do want to give it up. Let me tell you straight, today I want to give it all up."

"And I am telling you too." Picking up his own refrain, Swamishri carried the conversation forward. The youth was now talking with Swamishri with his head bowed. Swamishri first raised his head with his own hand and looked him in the eyes. Starting with a question, he said, "Do you feel there is any need for this?"
"No, no, let me tell you straight, there is no need at all."
"Then resolve that today you will give it up."
"I have given it up. Let me tell you straight, I am not going to drink any more."

"Then God will give you strength." Swamishri was speaking to him with just as much faith. For those around it was a spectacle, but Swamishri was trying very seriously to free him from this vice. Often Swamishri would ask one thing and his answer would be something else. Even so, repeating the question again and again, he was asking him for information.
"What do you do?"
"Bapji! My father lives in Atlanta."
"I am asking you what you do."
Swamishri asked him again. So the other man who had come with him said, "Right now he is with me at the motel."
"How much do you earn?"
When Swamishri asked this, he said, "My father has a stall."
Swamishri said, "I am asking you how much you earn here at the motel."
"It must be about four thousand dollars a month."
"And how much do you spend on drink?"
"Three thousand."

As if stunned by such a carefree answer, Swamishri looked at him for a moment. Then he said to the sadhus standing around, "He spends three thousand on alcohol, and then how much is left to run the house?!"
"A thousand," he answered again, just as cheerfully.
Patting his shoulder, Swamishri said, "From now on give it up, and come here to satsang."

He had a kanthi tied by Swamishri's hand. To meet with such faith this youth who had come in a drunken state, not even knowing what he was saying before Swamishri, to talk to him about giving up his addiction and to care about his future: only Swamishri can do this. There is no limit to his patience and compassion.

2006.o: Yagna for World Peace, Nagar Yatra
w: The yagna, under the auspices of the pratishtha rituals, had 1501 participants (Yajmans) seated around 187 yagna kunds with 110 Brahmins pundits performing the rituals. There were an additional 11 main yagna kunds on stage with 105 participants. Swamishri performed the panchamrut rituals on Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and thereafter he blessed the assembly, “The yagna has commenced for the murti-pratishtha ceremony. It is also a yagna for world peace. Hindu dharma is very charitable and perseveres for the good of all. It seeks to elevate and bestow moksha to all animals and humans. People may say that there is no peace in India. But to live amidst difficulties is indeed God’s grace and protection. By performing such yagnas we seek to be blessed with God’s grace, happiness and to become brahmarup...” Swamishri then performed the pujan and arti rituals of the murtis to be installed in the shikharbaddh mandir, namely, Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Ghanshyam Maharaj, Harikrishna Maharaj, Radha Krishna Dev, Ram Panchayatan, Shiv Panchayatan and Guru Parampara. Twenty-one thousand devotees and well-wishers came for darshan of the yagna and partook of the mahaprasad.

At 4.30 pm a grand procession (nagar yatra) of the murtis was carried out on the streets of Bhavnagar. The colourful pageant of devotion and its various attractions attracted the city dwellers, inspiring joy and devotion in their hearts.

Prior to the grand murti-pratishtha ceremony day of BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Bhadra, a yagna for World Peace was held from 9.00 a.m. In the evening a colourful procession of the murtis was held in the village. See details in Swaminarayan Bliss, June 2010.
Pramukh Swami Maharaj called Dharmakunvar Swami, Gnanprasad Swami and Narayanmuni Swami and gave guidance on who was to be seated in the helicopter.
Swamishri also enquired minutely about the ceremony to be held this evening to honour all those who had helped in the work of the mandir.
Swamishri said, "Have you decided which shawl is to be draped over whom and who will drape it? Have you made a list?"
However, no list had been made, so Swamishri said, "Meet Akshaymuni, Manish, Sanjay and others, prepare a list, and come and show it to me at five o'clock."
Then, as he got up for his walk, Swamishri said to Dharmacharan Swami, "Was Chunibhai Chaturvedi seated at the yagna?"
Dharmacharan Swami said, "All the arrangements had been made for him, but I do not know whether he sat or not."
Swamishri said, "Find out."
In this way, throughout the festival, Swamishri's insistence on precision in even the smallest matter kept making every task and arrangement shine all the more.
During a conversation, Abhayswarup Swami, kothari of the Mumbai mandir, said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "When your name is mentioned, all the work gets done."
Swamishri said, "Not my name, Shriji Maharaj's name."
Swamishri's devotion as a servant to his chosen deity shone through.
Talking about the youth activities going on in England, Anandpriya Swami said, "As you inspired, a programme of teaching Gujarati to the youth mandal is also running in the UK."

On hearing this, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Wonderful! The practice of Gujarati should keep going continuously, otherwise they will forget. The programme has been set up, but it should not be that they learn it and then forget it again. If we keep it going continuously, it will become firm. Let them speak a little in the assembly, speak for about five minutes in Gujarati; do it like that."
Swamishri, a strong promoter of the Gujarati language in India and abroad, has always welcomed and praised such programmes with enthusiasm.
Pramukh Swami Maharaj called Dharmakunvar Swami, Gnanprasad Swami and Narayanmuni Swami and gave guidance on who should be seated in the helicopter.
Moreover, Swamishri also asked in detail about the ceremony to be held this evening to honour all who had helped in the work of the mandir.
Swamishri said, "Has it all been decided which shawl is to be placed on whom and who will place it? Have you made a list?"
However, no list had been made, so Swamishri said, "Meet Akshaymuni, Manish, Sanjay and the others, prepare a list, and come and show it to me at five o'clock."
Then, getting up for his walk, Swamishri said to Dharmacharan Swami, "Was Chunibhai Chaturvedi seated at the yagna?"
Dharmacharan Swami said, "All arrangements have been made for him, but I do not know whether he sat or not."
Swamishri said, "Check it."

This evening Mahant Swami Maharaj himself expressed a wish: "Come, let us go and have darshan of Thakorji's thal..." Saying this, he went to where the thal is offered to Thakorji. He joined in singing the thal with devotion and then left. Everyone later understood the reason why Swamishri had suddenly gone for Thakorji's darshan.

What had happened was that a boy named Om Patel, studying in the seventh standard, had come to the mandir this morning for Swamishri's darshan. Swamishri usually gives darshan from the balcony between 7.00 and 7.20. But today he had gone early. And by 7.10 he had gone into his room. So this boy did not get darshan. He was close to tears. Divyaratnadas Swami said, "Swami gives darshan every day now! Come again tomorrow."
He said, "But Swami! I have English speaking and swimming classes during the vacation now; Thursday is the only day off..."
Finding a way, Divyaratnadas Swami said, "Then let me give you darshan of Swami's Harikrishna Maharaj..."

He told him the glory of Harikrishna Maharaj. The boy agreed, but before that he went to see his mother... The thought had come to him, "I will stay the whole day; perhaps I will get Swami's darshan." His mother said yes. He stayed. The sadhus showed him Thakorji's room. With devotion he had darshan of Thakorji's breakfast, midday meal and fruit offering. He prayed... and at night too he came and sat for the thal.

After a little while, Swamishri arrived. He came and stood right beside him. It was as if he had won the lottery. Seizing the chance, he even touched his feet... His joy knew no bounds. Swamishri had come of his own accord just to fulfil his wish. (Two days later, confirming this, Swamishri said, "I never go out at that time.")
